chief_complaint: severe throbbing unilateral headache with nausea
hpi_details: A 23-year-old male presents to the clinic with severe throbbing unilateral headache with nausea. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: He thinks the pounding pain was triggered by severe dehydration and drinking multiple energy drinks during his late work shifts.
concerns: He is worried that a blood vessel in his brain is leaking or about to burst like what happened to his uncle.
expectations: He hopes to get a brain CT scan to make sure there is no bleeding and something to stop the intense nausea.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Migraine without Aura evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Migraine without Aura is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Migraine without Aura: Triptans, dark room rest, avoid triggers, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Migraine without Aura.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Tension headache without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

Ignoring critical warning signs such as: sudden 'thunderclap' headache reaching peak intensity within seconds, new headache in a patient over 50, a change in a pre-existing headache pattern, headache with fever, neck stiffness, focal neurological deficits, or papilloedema.
management_principles: Plan for Migraine without Aura: Triptans, dark room rest, avoid triggers
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Migraine without Aura
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Migraine without Aura

teaching.one_liner: A recurrent throbbing, unilateral headache with nausea, often triggered by stress, chocolate, or red wine.
red_flags: Sudden 'thunderclap' headache reaching peak intensity within seconds — must exclude subarachnoid haemorrhage
New headache in a patient over 50, or a change in a pre-existing headache pattern — warrants imaging
Headache with fever, neck stiffness, focal neurological deficits, or papilloedema — raises concern for meningitis, mass lesion, or raised intracranial pressure

must_ask.say: Is the pain throbbing and one-sided?
Does stress, chocolate, or wine trigger it?
How long does each headache last?

history.answer: My head on the right side has been throbbing really badly since yesterday, and I feel nauseous.
It started gradually yesterday morning and built up over a few hours; it definitely didn't hit like a sudden thunderclap or lightning bolt.
The pain started yesterday morning, so it has been going on for about thirty hours now; I've had mild headaches a couple of times a year before, but this is the first time it has been this intense.
It is focused mostly on the right side of my head, around my temple and behind my right eye.
It is a pulsing, throbbing pain, like a heartbeat pounding in my temple, and at its worst it gets to about an 8 out of 10.
The throbbing has been pretty continuous since yesterday, and it gets especially worse when I move around or during the afternoon.
Walking around, climbing stairs, or bending over makes the throbbing much worse; resting quietly in a dark, quiet room helps take the edge off.
No, I didn't see any flashing lights, zigzag lines, or blind spots before the pain began, and I had no tingling or numbness.
Yes, I feel very nauseous and lost my appetite completely, though I haven't actually thrown up; bright lights and loud noises also bother me terribly.
No, my right eye isn't tearing up or red, my eyelid isn't drooping, and my nose isn't runny or stuffy.
No, I haven't had any fever, chills, neck stiffness, or skin rashes.
No, I haven't experienced any weakness, numbness, slurred speech, confusion, or seizures.
No, my vision is fine without any blurriness or double vision, and my eyes don't hurt to touch.
No, I haven't bumped or injured my head recently.
I took two tablets of over-the-counter acetaminophen yesterday evening, but it barely helped at all, and I only take painkillers maybe once every few months.
I've been under a lot of deadline stress at work this week, barely slept, and had red wine and dark chocolate with a friend two nights ago.
No, I don't have high blood pressure, and I don't take any blood pressure pills or blood thinners.
No, no one at home has a headache, and we don't use any unvented gas or charcoal heating appliances.
No, I don't have cancer, HIV, or any condition that affects my immune system.
I thought maybe chugging energy drinks and barely drinking any water during my night shifts brought this on.

I'm terrified that a blood vessel in my head is about to rupture, just like the aneurysm my uncle had a few years ago. I'm hoping I can get a quick head scan to prove nothing is bleeding inside, and some medicine to stop me from vomiting.
I don't have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes, kidney disease, or asthma.
I have never had any surgeries and I've never been admitted to a hospital.
I don't take any regular prescribed medications, vitamins, or herbal supplements.
I don't have any known allergies to foods or medications.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used vape products.
I only drink socially, maybe one or two glasses of beer or wine once or twice a month.
I work as a software junior developer and live alone in an apartment.
My mother occasionally gets bad throbbing headaches with nausea, but no one in my family has had aneurysms or brain tumors.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, pulse 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, temperature 36.6°C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert young male resting quietly in discomfort, shielding eyes slightly from bright light; no acute distress.
Pupils are equal, round, and reactive to light and accommodation; visual fields full to confrontation; fundoscopy shows sharp optic disc margins with no papilledema or retinal hemorrhage.
No tenderness over the frontal or maxillary sinuses.
Supple neck with full active range of motion; no Kernig sign or Brudzinski sign elicited.
Cranial nerves II through XII are grossly intact; facial symmetry preserved, extraocular movements intact without ptosis.
Normal bulk and tone; muscle strength 5/5 across all muscle groups in upper and lower extremities symmetrically.
Intact light touch and pinprick sensation throughout face and all four limbs symmetrically.
Biceps, triceps, patellar, and Achilles reflexes 2+ bilaterally; bilateral plantar responses are flexor (negative Babinski).
Finger-to-nose and heel-to-shin testing normal bilaterally; normal steady gait and negative Romberg sign.
